name: Viking Holdings Ltd
moat_justification: Strong premium brand in destination-focused cruising for affluent 55+ travelers: #1-rated river and ocean product, direct distribution, identical-ship fleet design that lowers unit costs, advance-booking visibility (96% of 2026 core capacity booked at Q2 2026, 2027 advance bookings ahead of prior year) and proven pricing power (Q2 2026 net yield +6.2% YoY, revenue +16.5% YoY) with high reported returns on invested capital (45.8% for FY2025 on the company's own non-IFRS calc in the 20-F) — capped at moderate-strong because cruising has no network effects or switching costs (guests re-shop every voyage against Royal Caribbean, Norwegian, Oceania/Regent and river rivals), the fleet advantage is bought with replicable shipbuilding capital rather than owned, demand is discretionary and cyclical (COVID-era losses, low-water disruption on European rivers in 2026), and growth requires continuous heavy vessel capex funded partly with debt. A 6 gives CAP 9.8 years.

WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Premium cruise brand with proven pricing power, moat 6/10 — but on the standardized total-capex OE base ($2.84/sh median) the weighted IRR is 9.61% (IV@15% $43.23 vs $82.60 price), so it clears 15% only below ~$43; confidence low — the median base is conservatively understated by the single-value capex override and no IFRS TTM pin exists.
moat_for: Premium brand and product ratings — #1 for Rivers and Oceans (Conde Nast Readers' Choice, five consecutive years per company reporting), destination-focused 'Thinking Person' positioning for affluent 55+ travelers
Proven pricing power — Q2 2026 net yield +6.2% YoY on top of capacity growth; FY2025 revenue +21.9%
Booking visibility — 96% of 2026 core capacity booked at Q2 2026; 2027 advance bookings pacing ahead of the prior season

Identical-ship fleet design — standardized river and ocean ships lower crew training, maintenance and inventory costs; young fleet keeps maintenance capex low (company-defined Ongoing Capex only $135.1M in FY2025)
High returns on capital — ROIC 45.8% for FY2025 on the company's own 20-F non-IFRS calculation
Direct sales channel and loyal repeat-guest base in a demographic (affluent retirees) with growing wealth and leisure time
moat_against: No network effects or switching costs — guests re-shop each voyage; Royal Caribbean, Norwegian, premium lines (Oceania/Regent) and river rivals compete for the same affluent traveler
Fleet advantage is replicable capital, not owned — any well-funded rival can order similar ships; growth requires ~$1B/yr of vessel capex
Discretionary, cyclical demand — travel spending falls in recessions and stops in crises (COVID-era losses; FY2023 net loss on derivative marks shows the leveraged history)

Environmental/operational exposure — historically low European river water levels disrupted over 50% of river capacity PCDs in Q3 2026; fuel and emissions-regulation costs sit outside management control

Leverage and sponsor history — net debt $1,698,031,000 at FY2025 (dcf_numbers.json) after a leveraged pre-IPO capital structure; share count rose with preference conversions and equity issuance (diluted shares 446,418,000 in FY2025 vs 221,936,000 in FY2023 on the engine history, a basis break from the Series C conversion at IPO)
